# hexdump

Inspect binary data as formatted text through MoonX.

## Usage

```sh
moonx cli/hexdump -C input.bin

moonx cli/hexdump -n 32 input.bin
```

Read files or stdin. Use canonical hex/ASCII output or the supported custom format strings.

## Common options

<!-- BEGIN GENERATED OPTIONS -->
<!-- Generated by tools/metadata from options.json. -->

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-C`, `--canonical` | hexadecimal bytes with ASCII |
| `-e VALUE`, `--format VALUE` | add a custom format |
| `-n VALUE`, `--length VALUE` | display at most N input bytes |
| `-s VALUE`, `--skip VALUE` | skip N input bytes Default: `0`. |
| `-v`, `--no-squeezing` | display duplicate blocks |
| `-h`, `--help` | Show help. |
| `-V`, `--version` | Show the version. |
<!-- END GENERATED OPTIONS -->

Use `--help` for the complete option list.

## Notes

Compatible with the MoonBit 2026-11-17 toolchain.

- Numeric formats use the fixed Linux profile and C locale. Forward offsets on non-seekable stdin are a project extension.

See the [compatibility guide](../../docs/compatibility.md) for the supported profile.
